public_rationale: Read as a summary of late 2024, the claim fits the evidence. In CNBC's October 2024 survey of tech leaders, 79% of firms used Copilot. A third of companies were still in the testing phase, and half of respondents said it was too soon to know whether it was worth the cost. That is adoption paired with wait-and-see. Nationally, the St. Louis Fed found that generative AI uptake two years after launch outpaced that of PCs and the internet, so it was not being ignored. One caveat: about 60% of US adults aged 18 to 64 had not used it as of August 2024. The 'waiting to see' part is best shown for businesses, not for the whole public.
limitations: 'People' is undefined; the strongest evidence covers businesses.
No direct measure of non-users' reasons for not using it.
The CNBC sample is small and not representative.
